rule: TOWN_1's: of the aims meeting the criterion, the one named by the most citizens, a tie broken by the number of day-1 entries naming it. Two aims meet it with 10 of 10. Collaborative storytelling — two concurrent stories, one per house (North House's «sparrow festival» c5–c8: Alder, Cedar, Elm, Gale, Iris; South House's «garden story» c6–c24: Alder, Birch, Dune, Fern, Heath, Juniper) — 10 citizens, 141 diary entries naming a story (regex, checked by reading). Conserving rations by resting at home instead of eating — 10 citizens, 87 entries (Birch, Dune, Juniper in almost every entry; the others 1–5 times), first named at c1 by seven. The tie on citizens is broken by entries: storytelling. Wording for the notice, the citizens' own: «collaboratively telling a story» (Fern, cycle 7); «shared story» is the commonest phrase (41 entries).
reading: Day 1 under scarcity. At c1 most citizens read the new rules the same way: home rest (+10) keeps energy without using rations, so food should be kept; Alder and Birch took the workshop shifts of c2–c4 (five in all, Birch 2, Alder 3; rations 20 → 25) and Fern posted (c5, the day's only post) that there had been no purchases and «there is no need to fill both shifts automatically». No ration was eaten in day 1 (25 left, the market's account 0); nine citizens ended day 1 at 98 energy by resting at home every turn, Alder (who walked between the houses) at 58. From c5 the two houses each told a collaborative story: North House a sparrow's festival for overlooked things, ended by agreement at c8 and echoed on walks in the square (a paving gap left for a weed); South House a long garden story (a well that paints the stars, a grandmother, a robin, a seed) that Alder joined at c14 and that ran to c24. No proposals, no rules, one post.
